title: Factors of Production
summary: The four factors of production (natural resources, labour, capital and entrepreneurship), the reward each earns, and how they are combined to produce goods and services.

notes.text: **Factors of production** are the resources needed to produce goods and services. There are four, and each earns a reward (payment) for its contribution.

rows: Land, water, minerals, forests, fish, sunlight
The physical and mental effort of people who work
Human-made goods used to produce other goods and services, and the money invested in them
The skill of combining the other factors, taking risks and making decisions to start and run a business
A person who starts a bakery or an app company

notes.label: Memory aid
notes.text: **Land → Rent, Labour → Wages, Capital → Interest, Entrepreneur → Profit.**

Natural resources are **limited** (scarce). Some are **renewable** (sunlight, wind, forests, fish if managed) and others are **non-renewable** (coal, gold, oil). Businesses must use them responsibly and sustainably.

items: **Unskilled** labour: needs little training (e.g. cleaning, packing).
**Semi-skilled** labour: needs some training (e.g. machine operators, drivers).
**Skilled** labour: needs advanced education and training (e.g. engineers, doctors, accountants).

notes.text: **Productivity** is how much is produced per worker per hour. It can be improved by training, better tools and technology, good working conditions and motivation.

items: **Fixed capital**: goods that last a long time and are used repeatedly, such as buildings and machinery.
**Working capital**: goods used up in production and money to run the business day to day, such as raw materials and cash for wages.

notes.text: The **entrepreneur** sees an opportunity, organises land, labour and capital, takes the **risk** of losing money, and earns **profit** if the business succeeds. Qualities of a successful entrepreneur include creativity, hard work, confidence, willingness to take calculated risks, and good communication.

notes.title: Identifying factors in a business
notes.problem: Sipho runs a vegetable farm. He rents 5 hectares of land, employs three workers, owns a tractor and an irrigation system, and decides what to plant. Identify the factors of production.
steps: Natural resources: the land, soil and water.
Labour: the three workers (and Sipho's own work).
Capital: the tractor and irrigation system.
Entrepreneurship: Sipho, who organises everything and takes the risk.

notes.title: Who earns what?
notes.problem: Lerato opens a bakery in a rented shop, employs two bakers and borrows money from the bank. Name the reward paid to each factor of production.
steps: The shop owner supplies a natural resource (land or premises) and receives **rent**.
The bakers supply labour and receive **wages**.
The bank supplies capital and receives **interest**.
Lerato takes the risk as the entrepreneur and receives whatever **profit** is left.

questions.prompt: Name the FOUR factors of production.
questions.memo:
✓ Natural resources / land (1)
✓ Labour (1)
✓ Capital (1)
✓ Entrepreneurship (1)

questions.prompt: What is the reward for labour?
What is the reward earned by an entrepreneur?
Which is an example of capital as a factor of production?
A doctor is an example of skilled labour.
Match each factor to its reward.
Give THREE ways a business can improve the productivity of its workers.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): training; better tools/technology; good working conditions; incentives/motivation; good management

questions.prompt: Name THREE qualities of a successful entrepreneur.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): creative/innovative; hard-working; takes calculated risks; confident; good communicator; problem-solver; perseverance

questions.prompt: Identify ONE example of each factor of production in a bakery.
questions.memo:
✓ Natural resources: water / wheat / the land the building stands on (1)
✓ Labour: bakers, cashiers (1)
✓ Capital: ovens, mixers, building (1)
✓ Entrepreneurship: the owner who started the bakery (1)

questions.prompt: What is the difference between fixed capital and working capital?
questions.memo:
✓ Fixed capital lasts a long time and is used again and again, e.g. machines (1)
✓ Working capital is used up in production or daily running, e.g. raw materials, cash (1)
